# clean taxonomy: pull taxa names & build dict of synonyms

## load packages

```{julia}
using CSV, DataFrames
using JLD2
using GeoIO, GeoStats
include("../../niche-modeling-utils/scripts/checklistutils.jl")
```

## load in taxa list df

We're only focusing on clade 1 (south) + 2b (central-northish), so let's filter down to that clade.

```{julia}
taxa_traits = DataFrame(CSV.File("data/taxonomy_trait_data/SupTable4-TraitsSpecies.csv"))
#clean up column names - change from all caps to lowercase
rename!(lowercase, taxa_traits)
#remove spaces
rename!(x -> replace(x, ' ' => '_'), taxa_traits)
filter!(:clade => x -> x == "1" || x == "2b", taxa_traits)
```

```{julia}
rename!(taxa_traits, Dict(:species => "scientificName"))
scientificName = replace.(taxa_traits.scientificName, "C. " => "Calceolaria ")
taxa_traits.scientificName = scientificName
#make a specificEpithet col
specificEpithet      = [split(taxa, " ")[2] for taxa in scientificName]
#make an infraspecificEpithet col (splitting on var. or subsp.)
infraspecificEpithet = Vector{Union{String,Missing}}()
for taxa in scientificName
    parts = split(taxa, " ")
    if length(parts) >= 4
        push!(infraspecificEpithet, parts[4])
    else
        push!(infraspecificEpithet, missing)
    end
end

insertcols!(taxa_traits, 2, :specificEpithet => specificEpithet)
insertcols!(taxa_traits, 3, :infraspecificEpithet => infraspecificEpithet)
```

## load in powo checklist

build a Kew / Plants of the World Online checklist with `build_checklist` (from `niche-modeling-utils`), including each
accepted name's native range at the botanical country level.
we ask for the whole family rather than just *Calceolaria*, so we also get the synonyms that were described in other
genera (ex. "Fagelia biflora").

this queries POWO, so the names can change between runs: only re-run this chunk when you want to update the checklist.

```{julia}
#| eval: false
checklist_path = "data/taxonomy_trait_data/powo_checklist.csv"
build_checklist("Calceolariaceae"; output_file=checklist_path)
```

```{julia}
checklist_path = "data/taxonomy_trait_data/powo_checklist.csv"
checklist = DataFrame(CSV.File(checklist_path))
```

### compare names from anahí with powo valid names

```{julia}
validnames = checklist.name[checklist.accepted]

discrepancies = String[]
for name in scientificName
    if name ∉ validnames
        push!(discrepancies, name)
    end
end

discrepancies
```

### reconcile discrepancies with powo

1.  "Calceolaria ascendens subsp. exigua” —> Kew says this is a synonym for "Calceolaria ascendens subsp. glandulifera"
>> This one is C. ascendens glandulifera
we already have C. ascendens glandulifera in the df, so let's delete this line.

```{julia}
#delete this entry from df
deleteat!(taxa_traits, findall(==("Calceolaria ascendens subsp. exigua"), taxa_traits.scientificName))
```

2.  "Calceolaria petiolaris” —> Kew says this is a synonym for “C. petioalaris"
>> You're right. This is a typo. It is C. petioalaris

```{julia}
#replace petiolaris with "petioalaris"
replace!(taxa_traits.scientificName, "Calceolaria petiolaris" => "Calceolaria petioalaris")
replace!(taxa_traits.specificEpithet, "petiolaris" => "petioalaris")
```

3.  "Calceolaria corymbosa subsp. montana” —> Kew says this is a synonym for "Calceolaria mollissima"
>> The right species to use here is C. corymbosa montana (mollissima is an old name)

instead of changing the dataframe, I'll look this one up under "Calceolaria mollissima" in the POWO checklist (see `powo_names` below).

4.  "Calceolaria crenatifolia”  —> Kew doesn’t have anything for “crenatifolia”, but they do have “crenatiflora” accepted
>> Another typo. This is C. crenatiflora indeed.

```{julia}
#replace crenatifolia with "crenatiflora"
replace!(taxa_traits.scientificName, "Calceolaria crenatifolia" => "Calceolaria crenatiflora")
replace!(taxa_traits.specificEpithet, "crenatifolia" => "crenatiflora")
```

5.  "Calceolaria corymbosa subsp. santiagana” —> I think you have a typo, should be "santiagina"
>> Another typo. This is C. corymbosa santiagina (with an "i")

```{julia}
#replace santiagana with "santiagina"
replace!(taxa_traits.scientificName, "Calceolaria corymbosa subsp. santiagana" => "Calceolaria corymbosa subsp. santiagina")
replace!(taxa_traits.infraspecificEpithet, "santiagana" => "santiagina")
```

6.  "Calceolaria dentata subsp. cummingiana” —> Kew has one m in “cumingiana” but on the internet I see 2 ms (“cummingiana”) in other sources
>> This one is C. dentata cummingiana (with two "m"s)

so, two of our names differ from the accepted POWO names: let's keep track of which POWO name to look them up under.
for cummingiana, let's also manually add our spelling to its synonyms to cover our bases.

the checklist is built from names in Calceolariaceae, so it misses the two synonyms that were described in *Boea*
(which POWO files under another family): let's add those manually too.

```{julia}
# our name => accepted POWO name
powo_names = Dict(
    "Calceolaria dentata subsp. cummingiana" => "Calceolaria dentata subsp. cumingiana",
    "Calceolaria corymbosa subsp. montana" => "Calceolaria mollissima"
)

# our name => synonyms to add on top of the POWO ones
manual_synonyms = Dict(
    "Calceolaria dentata subsp. cummingiana" => [("Calceolaria dentata subsp. cummingiana", "(Witasek) C.Ehrh.")],
    "Calceolaria biflora" => [("Boea plantaginea", "(Sm.) Pers.")],
    "Calceolaria petioalaris" => [("Boea alata", "Pers.")]
)
```

## gather my valid names vs. synonyms & their authorities

### get species authorities for valid names

```{julia}
# valid name => authority, for all valid names (including those we don't have sampled)
authority_dict = Dict(row.name => row.author for row in eachrow(checklist) if row.accepted && !ismissing(row.author))

# Add speciesAuthority column to taxa_traits
taxa_traits.speciesAuthority = [get(authority_dict, name, missing) for name in taxa_traits.scientificName]
```

### build our synonym dictionary (mapping valid names to synonyms)

`checklist_synonyms` gives us the accepted name + every synonym that points to it, each with its authority.

```{julia}
synonymdict = Dict{String, Vector{Tuple{String, Union{String, Missing}}}}()

for name in taxa_traits.scientificName
    syns = vcat(get(manual_synonyms, name, []), checklist_synonyms(checklist, get(powo_names, name, name)))

    # our name goes first (it's used as the accepted name when cleaning occurrences)
    ours = filter(syn -> first(syn) == name, syns)
    synonymdict[name] = unique(vcat(isempty(ours) ? [(name, missing)] : ours, syns))
end

# preview synonyms
for k in sort(collect(keys(synonymdict)))
    if length(synonymdict[k]) > 1
        @show k synonymdict[k]
    end
end
```

### build a species-level synonym dictionary for taxa sampled at the infraspecific level

for every taxon we sampled at the infraspecific level (ex. "Calceolaria meyeniana subsp. meyeniana"),
we also want to be able to pull occurrences at the specific level ("Calceolaria meyeniana").
`synonymdict` only has the synonyms of the infraspecific taxa we sampled, so pooling those misses:

- the species name itself,
- the accepted infraspecific taxa of that species that we *didn't* sample (ex. "Calceolaria meyeniana subsp. glabrata"),
- synonyms of the species as a whole & of those unsampled infraspecific taxa.

so, let's build `species_synonymdict`, mapping each species-level name to everything POWO places
under that species (at any rank), plus what we gathered in `synonymdict` for our sampled infraspecific taxa
(ex. "Calceolaria mollissima" for corymbosa, the "cummingiana" spelling for dentata).

```{julia}
# species-level name => infraspecific taxa we sampled
species_to_infrataxa = Dict{String, Vector{String}}()
for row in eachrow(taxa_traits)
    ismissing(row.infraspecificEpithet) && continue
    sp_name = "Calceolaria $(row.specificEpithet)"
    push!(get!(species_to_infrataxa, sp_name, String[]), row.scientificName)
end

species_synonymdict = Dict{String, Vector{Tuple{String, Union{String, Missing}}}}()

for (sp_name, infrataxa) in species_to_infrataxa
    # the species itself, all of its accepted infraspecific taxa (sampled or not), & all of their synonyms
    syns = checklist_synonyms(checklist, sp_name; include_infraspecific=true)

    # everything we already gathered (incl. manual additions) for the infraspecific taxa we sampled
    for infrataxon in infrataxa
        append!(syns, synonymdict[infrataxon])
    end

    species_synonymdict[sp_name] = unique(syns)
end

# preview species-level synonyms
for k in sort(collect(keys(species_synonymdict)))
    println(k, " (", length(species_synonymdict[k]), " names; sampled: ", join(species_to_infrataxa[k], ", "), ")")
    for (syn_name, syn_auth) in species_synonymdict[k]
        println("    ", syn_name, "  ", coalesce(syn_auth, ""))
    end
end
```

### find homonyms

some names are used for more than one taxon, under different authorities:

- a name can be both accepted & a synonym of something else (ex. "Calceolaria glandulosa Poepp. ex Benth." is accepted,
  while "Calceolaria glandulosa Benth." is a synonym of "Calceolaria nitida"),
- a name can be a synonym of two different accepted taxa (ex. "Calceolaria cheiranthoides Reiche ex Witasek" is a synonym of
  "Calceolaria meyeniana subsp. cheiranthoides", while "Calceolaria cheiranthoides Phil. ex Reiche" is a synonym of
  "Calceolaria dentata subsp. dentata").

`checklist_homonyms` finds all of these. Note, some of these names may not be valid names that *we have sampled*, but they
may be a synonym to one we have sampled (ex. Calceolaria hypoleuca Kraenzl. is a synonym of Calceolaria soratensis Kraenzl.).

```{julia}
homonym_df = checklist_homonyms(checklist)
```

### filter homonym_df to only include species of interest

now, we can filter the `homonym_df` to only include values in our synonym dictionary.
```{julia}
synonymdict_values = Set{String}()
for (key, value_list) in synonymdict
    for (syn_name, syn_auth) in value_list
        push!(synonymdict_values, syn_name)
    end
end
# also keep homonyms relevant to the species-level pulls
for (key, value_list) in species_synonymdict
    for (syn_name, syn_auth) in value_list
        push!(synonymdict_values, syn_name)
    end
end

homonym_df = filter(homonym_df) do row
    name_match = row.scientificName in synonymdict_values
    valid_match = !ismissing(row.validName) && row.validName in synonymdict_values
    name_match || valid_match
end
```

## gather native ranges from checklist 

```{julia}
# taxon -> botanical country codes
# (looking up the taxa where we're using a different name under their valid POWO name)
country_dict = Dict(
    name => checklist_native_range(checklist, get(powo_names, name, name))
    for name in taxa_traits.scientificName
)

# Add to taxa_traits dataframe
taxa_traits.botanicalCountries = [country_dict[name] for name in taxa_traits.scientificName]
```

### gather native ranges for the species-level taxa

for the taxa we sampled at the infraspecific level, we also pull occurrences at the specific level (see `species_synonymdict`),
so let's get the native range of the species as a whole: the species itself + all of its accepted infraspecific taxa (sampled or not).

```{julia}
species_country_dict = Dict{String, Vector{String}}()

for (sp_name, infrataxa) in species_to_infrataxa
    country_codes = checklist_native_range(checklist, sp_name; include_infraspecific=true)

    # also cover the taxa where we're using a different name compared to the valid POWO names
    for infrataxon in infrataxa
        append!(country_codes, country_dict[infrataxon])
    end

    species_country_dict[sp_name] = sort(unique(country_codes))
end

species_ranges = DataFrame(scientificName = sort(collect(keys(species_country_dict))))
species_ranges.specificEpithet = [split(name, " ")[2] for name in species_ranges.scientificName]
species_ranges.botanicalCountries = [species_country_dict[name] for name in species_ranges.scientificName]
species_ranges
```

write out clean version of `taxa_traits`, my homonym df, my synonym dict, my species-level synonym dict & native ranges:
```{julia}
CSV.write("data/taxonomy_trait_data/species_level_ranges.csv", species_ranges)
save("data/taxonomy_trait_data/synonymdict.jld2", synonymdict)
save("data/taxonomy_trait_data/species_synonymdict.jld2", species_synonymdict)
CSV.write("data/taxonomy_trait_data/homonyms.csv", homonym_df)
CSV.write("data/taxonomy_trait_data/traits_species_cleaned-2026_02_25.csv", taxa_traits)
```
